Elena — thanks for the clear request. Short answers up front: we can consider extended terms with a credit review and supporting docs, and we can handle EU VAT via either a standard VAT invoice or reverse-charge documentation depending on Acme's preference and EU entity setup.

What we'll need to start a formal credit review:
- Completed Redwood credit application (I attached the form)
- Last two quarters of AP aging or a signed PO that guarantees payment cadence
- VAT registration copy for the EU entity (or confirmation of B2B reverse-charge setup)

On credit cap: our typical process is to provisionally grant a temporary cap for 1–2 invoices while the financial review completes; full increases are approved by Finance (Monica). If you need $250k immediately we can evaluate a provisional $150–200k with strict invoice milestones.

Proposed next steps:
1) Elena to share signed VAT doc and confirm preferred VAT treatment.
2) Acme to complete the attached redwood-credit-app.pdf and return to finance@redwood.ai.
3) Quick 20-min call tomorrow for cadence and PO timing — proposed 10:30am PT.

Cc'ing Monica for the credit assessment and Laura to track the PO and billing cadence.

—Karthik

Karthik — I ran a preliminary credit assessment on Acme using internal scoring and public filings. Key points:
- Historic payment behavior: generally strong, but Q4 usage spikes have produced higher APRs for vendor lines.
- For an immediate cap increase, recommend a provisional cap of $200,000 with staged release tied to payment performance (2x invoice clearance).
- Net60 is higher risk for us; we can offer Net45 for the first three invoices as a compromise, then move to Net60 once customer clears two consecutive invoices on time.

VAT notes: if Acme can confirm B2B reverse charge for the EU entity (valid VAT ID + signed attestation), Redwood will issue invoices without VAT and include the reverse-charge reference. If Acme prefers vendor-charged VAT, Treasury needs a copy of the VAT registration and monthly reconciliation samples.

Proposed payment schedule (internal recommendation):
- Invoice 1: Net45, release $100k of provisional cap
- Invoice 2: Net45, on-time = release additional $50k (cap $150k)
- Invoice 3: On-time = full cap $200k and evaluate for further increase after credit app review

I'll attach the completed internal scoring and the redwood-credit-app.pdf for their completion. We should push for PO + signed attestation before granting provisional cap.

Monica
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

Agreed provisional terms:
- Provisional credit cap: $200,000 (effective immediately upon signed agreement)
- Payment terms: Net45 for first three invoices. After two consecutive on-time payments Redwood will transition to Net60 for subsequent invoices.
- VAT handling: Redwood will issue VAT-exempt invoices under reverse-charge for Acme’s EU entity upon receipt of the EU VAT registration (vat-registration-acme.pdf) and a signed VAT attestation form. If Acme prefers Redwood to charge VAT, please state that explicitly and provide a monthly reconciliation template.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly invoices with invoice delivery on the 5th of each month and due dates adjusted to the Net45/Net60 schedule above. We will map invoice dates to your quarter-close if you provide the preferred PO numbers per period.

Required items to finalize and activate cap:
1) Completed redwood-credit-app.pdf (attached).
2) Signed VAT attestation and EU VAT registration (vat-registration-acme.pdf).
3) Signed DocuSign for provisional credit agreement (link to follow).

Next steps:

- Laura will coordinate PO numbers and the invoicing cadence once the agreement is signed.
